newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia coffee crop estimates cut to 8.3 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Colombia coffee crop estimates cut to 8.3 mln bags.

text.p: Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation forecast the 1996/97 crop would be about 8.3 million 60-kg bags, down from the most recent estimates of 10.4 million bags, a spokesman said Wednesday.
The plunging crop estimates would create a deficit of fresh coffee of at least 2.7 million 60-kg bags based on an export schedule of 11 million bags for 1996/97, the spokesman said.
Federation commercial manager John Naranjo referred last Friday to a "drastic drop" in the 1996/97 crop but said it would be about 10.4 million 60-kg bags.
Spokesman Romn Medina gave no immediate explanation for the sharp downward revision in less than one week.

Medina said the federation faced a serious deficit on export commitments and said it was proposing to swap 800,000 bags of old coffee from existing stocks for 600,000 bags of fresh excelso coffee from private exporters.
The private exporters said the proposal was made at a meeting last Monday with federation chief Jorge Crdenas.
Exporters said there was immediate agreement on the proposed swap but stressed contracts with roasters called for delivery of fresh coffee and not old.
As an alternative to the proposed swap, exporters said the federation had threatened to put a lien on 25 percent of their coffee in the 1996/97 year.
"The federation has no fresh coffee and has not been able to buy any," said one private exporter.
Naranjo said last Friday that the federation had six million 60-kg bags of coffee in its inventories and that "the majority of it is in excellent condition."
